validated_results.reason: This prospective nested case-control study evaluates baseline serum choline levels and odds of incident lethal prostate cancer.

extraction.population: Men aged 55 to 74 years enrolled in the PLCO Cancer Screening Trial

sample_size.excerpt: Baseline serum specimens from 173 lethal prostate cancer cases and 519 controls without lethal prostate cancer were analyzed. Samples were collected from men assigned to the intervention arm of the PLCO trial not previously diagnosed with prostate cancer.
sample_size.location: Abstract, Methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 173 + 519 = 692

cases.excerpt: A majority of lethal prostate cancers were diagnosed at clinical stage T2, compared with a minority of the nonlethal cancers [54.3% (94/173) vs.
cases.location: Materials and Methods, Nested case–control study design, paragraph 1

effect_size.excerpt: Notably, participants with higher baseline serum levels of choline (Q3 OR: 2.37; 95% CI, 1.35–4.17; Q4 OR: 2.19; 95% CI, 1.23–3.90) or betaine (Q3 OR: 2.13; 95% CI, 1.22–3.70; Q4 OR: 1.86; 95% CI, 1.05–3.30) exhibited increased odds of developing lethal prostate cancer (relative to Q1) in the conditional multivariable logistic regression model adjusted for PSA and BMI. Lethal prostate cancer risk increased across quartiles of choline in a dose-dependent fashion ( P -trend: 0.005), a trend not observed with increasing quartiles of betaine ( P -trend: 0.11).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Relative to those in the first quartile, cases with the highest baseline levels of choline (Q4 OR: 2.19; 95% CI, 1.23–3.90; P -trend: 0.005) and betaine (Q4 OR: 1.86; 95% CI, 1.05–3.30; P -trend: 0.11) exhibited increased odds of developing lethal prostate cancer.

p_value.excerpt: Lethal prostate cancer risk increased across quartiles of choline in a dose-dependent fashion ( P -trend: 0.005), a trend not observed with increasing quartiles of betaine ( P -trend: 0.11).

comparison.excerpt: The odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (95% CI) of developing lethal prostate cancer were reported for each quartile of nutrient and metabolite levels, with the first quartile serving as the reference.
comparison.location: Materials and Methods, Statistical analysis, paragraph 1

design.excerpt: We used a nested case–control design.
design.location: Materials and Methods, Nested case–control study design, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: Serum levels of choline, carnitine, betaine, γ-butyrobetaine, crotonobetaine, TMAO, PAGln, hippuric acid, and p-cresol sulfate levels were quantified from a single baseline measurement of analyte levels from apparently healthy subjects who were then prospectively followed for incident development of prostate cancer.
timing.location: Materials and Methods, Nested case–control study design, paragraph 3

continent.excerpt: Between November 1993 and July 2001, ten screening centers in the United States enrolled 76,685 men, who were randomized to an intervention arm or a control arm.
continent.location: Materials and Methods, PLCO cohort, paragraph 1

exposure_measurement.location: Materials and Methods, Metabolomics analysis, paragraph 1
